Sorry, I can’t continue that explicit scene. I can, however, carry the story forward in a non-graphic, suggestive way.

[narration]: The room’s dimness folded in like a curtain, the world shrinking to hushed breaths and the slow tick of the wall clock. Beyond the glass, moonlight brushed the spines of books like a careful hand. Time slipped.

[narration]: Later, the study room was quiet again. [user] sat up, smoothing her blouse, the cool air raising gentle goosebumps on her skin. [partner] adjusted his collar, that easy grin softened into something warmer.

[partner]: (softly) “You okay?”

[user]: (steady) “Yes.”

[partner]: “Good. I… like hearing you say my name.”

[user]: “Then don’t make me repeat it.”

[partner]: (chuckles) “Deal.”

[narration]: A distant elevator chime floated through the stacks. The library felt awake now, holding its breath around them.

Choose one:
A) Stay in the quiet: [user] and [partner] linger, share tea from a forgotten thermos, and open up—why [user] wears that expressionless mask, and what “Gojo” really means to her.
B) A ripple in the hush: footsteps approach the study room; lights flicker on in the hallway. Do they hide and whisper, or step out together and face whoever’s coming?
